label: a16-vs-a22in12-n2x2
_why: THE 2+1 TESTS (user-ruled 2026-09-13; HANDOVER session N+2): two arms, two runs each, alternating, on books regenerated by the ERA-KEYED generator after the era pass (BALANCE_FRAMEWORK §10.78) and the canon of the same evening (§10.78.1: motor [0,2,3] with the minted top rung dropped, munition [1,2], 56 buildings, 182 technologies). Arm 1 canon-flat-in12-a16 = the §10.77 flat-cost lifted book with the output step sized on the LIFTED era-0 rung: A 1.6 / B 1.5 (F97's death ratio — a rung two behind under 0.2 of the frontier's VA per worker — is reached at A ≈ 1.55–1.6 once era 0's inputs are ×1.2, not at 2.2; the frontier then earns vanilla's own margin and its VA per 1,000 construction points is ~2× vanilla's instead of F110's 14×). Arm 2 canon-je24-a22-in12 = phase 2's book (A 2.2, cost ×2.2^era, ai_value 3^era, divisor 0.000125, bar 24) plus the ×1.2 lift and NOTHING else — the control that isolates the death lever from cheap capital. After the four runs: per arm, the obsolescence composition (era-0 workforce 1900→1935, stale and frontier payback, staffing by era) and the GDP-productivity composition (GDP = pop × workers per capita × GDP per worker); if the two runs of an arm are well aligned the deduction stays, if they diverge a third run of that arm breaks the tie (see _alignment).

_delta: Arm 1 vs canon-flat-in12 (F110, n=1): A 1.6 in place of 2.2 — one lever. Arm 2 vs canon-je24-a22 (F109, n=11): the ×1.2 lift — one lever. ⚠ BOTH baselines were generated by the pre-era-pass generator: their automotive, munition, synthetics and electrics rungs were index-keyed (priced as 1836 rungs; electrics on e1). The test books carry those four industries at their ERAS (F111), so the arms are one-lever steps from their baselines on the thirteen four-method industries and on every world reading, and NOT on automobiles / telephones / dye / ammunition — read those four industries against vanilla, never against phase 2 or F110. ⚠ AND every secondary production method is dearer on rungs 1+ than in every measured book: emit_secondaries.mjs's input regex had shipped broken since 2026-09-01 (inputs at vanilla quantities, outputs scaled), fixed 2026-09-13 (BUGS_AND_FIXES) — a second change against both baselines, on secondary adoption (canneries, luxury lines, rayon, porcelain, radios), not on the main ladder. Motor is [0,2,3] in both arms (the canon's structure since the evening of 2026-09-13) against [0,1,2,3] with a minted top rung in both baselines: read motor and engines against vanilla as well.

_predictions.arm1_gdp: world GDP 0.9–1.3× the vanilla n=16 median at 1935 (above 1 likelier than below)
_predictions.arm1_workers: productive workers per capita 0.9–1.1× vanilla; unemployment 10–20% of salaried+unemployed (vanilla 16.3%, flat-in12 7.3%, a22 30.3%)
_predictions.arm1_capital: pools under 0.6 of a year's world GDP; construction sector 1–1.5× vanilla's levels
_predictions.arm1_obsolescence: era-0 tiered workforce falls 1900→1935 and the stale (e0) payback exceeds 30 y; below-best under 35% (risk: back toward 40% — the frontier's edge per construction point is 2× a rung, not 3×)
_predictions.arm1_perf_prices: row P total within ±10% of vanilla; groceries above 0.6 of vanilla's price
_predictions.arm2_obsolescence: era-0 workforce falls 1900→1935 and its payback exceeds 30 y — the lever works without cheap capital
_predictions.arm2_world: GDP 0.8–0.95×; workers per capita 0.6–0.7×; unemployment ~30%; pools 0.3–0.4 of world GDP; stall risk above a22's 2 of 11 (rung 0 loses money from 1836 at target_be ~123 and the first higher rungs arrive in the 1850s). One stall in two runs decides nothing at n=2 — say so.
_predictions.four_industries: automotive, electrics, synthetics, munition at their eras for the first time: their VA per staffed level within 0.5–2× their era peers (steel/arms of the same era) and their share of world VA back toward vanilla's 2%; telephones and automobiles no longer 12–17% above vanilla's price

_alignment: Per arm, run 1 against run 2 — ALL of: world GDP ÷ vanilla within 0.15 of each other AND on the same side of every G4 bound; productive workers per capita within 0.10; the era-0 workforce moving the same way 1900→1935; stale payback on the same side of 30 y; below-best within 5 pp. All hold ⇒ the arm's reading stands at n=2. Any fails ⇒ one more run of that arm (the tie-breaker), read the median of three. Two stalls in one arm are the arm's stall signature, not divergence: record, do not tie-break on them.
_comparison: vanilla n=16 (20260821_131149) is the reference for every ratio; F110 (canon-flat-in12, n=1) and F109 (canon-je24-a22, n=11) are the baselines each arm steps from (one lever each, with the _delta caveat); phase 1 (F107) for the stall census.
_watch: every run ~5 min in: mod marker, version, this run's error window by position, clock (batch_heartbeat.sh at each wake)
first run: first_run_decomp, je_tally, queue_mix; check rung-0 profits at 1840 against the lift
after run 10: an interim F108-style stall census (world GDP ÷ vanilla mean, GBR at 1935)
post-run: preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger with phase 2 as --nb
_cost: 4 × 1836→1936 ≈ 4 × 2h40–3h35 ≈ 12–14 h continuous, plus resumes; ~140 MB a run. Alternating so a Steam update or a slow night hits both arms.
_caveats: n=2 per arm by design; the alignment test above says whether that is enough.
The era pass changed the four late industries between the baselines and these books (see _delta).
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent; the five-minute smoke check on EVERY run; batch_heartbeat.sh at every wake.
